pluss::subsp::stats::ts::arch_lm¶

Engle’s ARCH-LM test for volatility clustering: are the squared values of a series autocorrelated?

Signature¶

ts::ArchLmResult ts::arch_lm(const pluss::Series& x, const ts::ArchLmOptions& options = {}, pluss::codem::Config cfg = {});

What It Does¶

arch_lm regresses the squared series on its own lags lagged values and reports n R² of that regression, which is chi-squared with lags degrees of freedom under the null of no ARCH effects. A series whose scale alternates between calm and turbulent stretches has autocorrelated squares and is rejected; steady noise is not. Rejection says that a constant-variance model is wrong and that a GARCH-type model of the variance is appropriate.

For a raw series leave demean on. If the input is already the residual vector of a mean model (whose mean is zero by construction), pass demean = false.

Parameters¶

const pluss::Series& x

A one-dimensional series in time order, at least two observations long.

const ts::ArchLmOptions& options

lags (default 1), demean (default true) and alpha (the significance level of the critical value, default 0.05); see ArchLmOptions.

pluss::codem::Config cfg

Output configuration (dtype and platform of the returned series); the computation itself runs in double precision.

Returns¶

An ArchLmResult: the statistic, the p-value, the critical value at alpha, reject, the degrees of freedom and the number of observations used.

Errors¶

  • lags must be at least 1 and smaller than the series length.

Practical Examples¶

Example 1¶

A series whose scale alternates between 0.3 and 2.0 every 50 observations is rejected; steady noise of the same overall size is not.

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const auto e = noise(300);
  std::vector<double> clustered(300), steady(300);
  for (int i = 0; i < 300; ++i) {
    const double scale = ((i / 50) % 2 == 0) ? 0.3 : 2.0;
    clustered[i] = scale * e[i];
    steady[i] = 1.2 * e[i];
  }
  ts::ArchLmOptions options;
  options.lags = 4;
  for (const auto* data : {&clustered, &steady}) {
    const auto r = ts::arch_lm(pluss::make_series(*data, {300}, f64), options);
    std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(3) << (data == &clustered ? "clustered" : "steady   ") << "  LM = " << r.stat << "  p = " << r.pvalue << "  critical = " << r.critical
              << "  reject = " << std::boolalpha << r.reject << "\n";
  }
}

Output

clustered  LM = 54.463  p = 0.000  critical = 9.488  reject = true
steady     LM = 4.789  p = 0.310  critical = 9.488  reject = false

Example 2¶

The result also reports the degrees of freedom and how many observations took part (the lags are used up by the regression).

#include <pluss/ma.h>

#include <cmath>
#include <iomanip>
#include <iostream>
#include <vector>

namespace ts = pluss::subsp::stats::ts;
using pluss::Series;

const auto f64 = pluss::Config{}.with_dtype(pluss::ScalarType::Float64);
void show(const char* label, const Series& s) {
  std::cout << std::left << std::setw(14) << label << std::right << std::fixed << std::setprecision(4);
  for (double v : s.host<double>()) std::cout << std::setw(9) << v;
  std::cout << "\n";
}
std::vector<double> noise(int n) {
  std::vector<double> e(n);
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    double u = std::sin(12.9898 * (i + 1.0) + 78.233) * 43758.5453;
    u -= std::floor(u);
    e[i] = u - 0.5;
  }
  return e;
}
Series ar1(int n, double phi) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double carry = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    carry = phi * carry + e[i];
    x[i] = carry;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}
Series walk(int n) {
  const auto e = noise(n);
  std::vector<double> x(n);
  double sum = 0.0;
  for (int i = 0; i < n; ++i) {
    sum += e[i];
    x[i] = sum;
  }
  return pluss::make_series(x, {n}, f64);
}

int main() {
  const auto e = noise(300);
  ts::ArchLmOptions options;
  options.lags = 4;
  const auto r = ts::arch_lm(pluss::make_series(e, {300}, f64), options);
  std::cout << "dof = " << r.dof << ", effective observations = " << r.effective_n << "\n";
}

Output

dof = 4, effective observations = 296
